title: Sea Ice
supports: Sea ice reflects more sunlight than open ocean; exposed water absorbs sunlight that can warm the upper ocean and reinforce melt. The page also explains the seasonal sunlight cycle and sea ice's insulating role.

title: Why Sea Ice Matters
publisher: National Snow and Ice Data Center
supports: Bright sea ice has higher albedo than surrounding ocean; when warming melts ice, the darker surface absorbs more heat and can amplify further melting.

title: Chapter 10: Linking Global to Regional Climate Change
supports: The IPCC AR6 WGI assessment identifies ice-albedo alongside lapse-rate, Planck, and cloud feedbacks among mechanisms associated with Arctic amplification.
